close_reason: Changed MdnSendRequest.on_success_update_email from HashMap<Id, PatchObject> to HashMap<String, PatchObject>. Reasoning: (1) the doc comment itself admitted keys can be '#creationId' references per RFC 8620 §5.7; (2) Id's contract (RFC 8620 §1.2: URL-safe base64 alphabet) forbids '#'; (3) jmap-types::SetResponse canonical pattern keys creation-id maps by String, real-id maps by Id (JMAP-zx3s.15 counter-research). Updated rustdoc on the field. Updated downstream jmap-mail-server::mdn.rs comments that incorrectly said 'patches is HashMap<Id, PatchObject>'. Updated the existing mdn_send_request_on_success_update_email_roundtrip test to use String key lookup instead of Id::from('#k1'). cargo test --workspace clean; cargo clippy --workspace clean.
description:
## Caller contract risk: the typed shape for \`on_success_update_email\` uses Id to hold values that Id's own type contract forbids.

This diff changed:

```rust
// Before
pub on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<String, Value>>,
// After
pub on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>,
```

with a doc comment that admits:

> Keys are Email IDs (or \`#creationId\` references resolved by the dispatcher); values are PatchObjects (RFC 8620 §5.3). Both [\`Id\`] and [\`PatchObject\`] are \`#[serde(transparent)]\`, so the wire format is byte-identical to a \`HashMap<String, Object>\`.

But \`Id\` is defined in \`jmap-types\` (\`crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:20-29\`) with the doc contract:

> Character set: URL-safe base64 alphabet (A-Za-z0-9, \`-\`, \`_\`), max 255 octets. Clients MUST treat Id values as opaque strings — no parsing of structure.

The character \`#\` is NOT in the URL-safe base64 alphabet. So per \`Id\`'s own type contract, \`Id::from(\"#k1\")\` produces an Id that violates the contract — and the type accepts it silently because \`From<String>\` performs no validation (only \`Id::new_validated\` does, and the diff does not use it).

### Two unresolved positions in the diff

The current code holds two contradictory positions:

1. \"\`on_success_update_email\` keys are \`Id\`\" — but Id's contract forbids \`#\`.
2. \"\`Id\` is just a String newtype with no validation\" — but Id's docstring says otherwise.

The diff's own test (\`mdn_send_request_on_success_update_email_roundtrip\`) calls \`Id::from(\"#k1\")\` and treats this as valid, leaning on position (2). The test passes because there is no validation. The doc contract on \`Id\`, written years before this change, leans on position (1).

### Why this matters for callers

A caller who reads the \`Id\` doc and writes a strict validator (\"only base64-URL chars, max 255 octets\") will reject \`#k1\` and fail to construct an \`on_success_update_email\` entry that the dispatcher actually accepts. A caller who notices the \`Id::from\` is permissive and ignores the doc loses the type-safety the \`Id\` newtype was intended to provide.

Either:

a. **Fix the \`Id\` doc** to say \"any non-empty string up to 255 octets, including the wire \`#\`-prefixed creation-id reference form per RFC 8620 §5.7\" — accepting that \`Id\` is wire-permissive. This is the realpolitik option but undermines the type-safety story of every other Id field in the workspace.

b. **Fix the \`on_success_update_email\` type** to admit creation-id references explicitly:

   ```rust
   pub enum EmailIdOrCreationRef {
       Real(Id),
       Creation(String), // wire form: \"#k1\"
   }
   pub on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<EmailIdOrCreationRef, PatchObject>>,
   ```

   Or revert to \`HashMap<String, PatchObject>\` (still typed-value but not lying about keys), matching the workspace pattern in \`SetResponse.not_created\` which uses \`HashMap<String, SetError>\` for the same creation-id shape.

The current type-the-doc-disagrees-with state is the worst of both worlds.

### Cross-references

- \`crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:20-29\` — Id type contract.
- \`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:282\` — workspace canonical \`HashMap<String, T>\` for creation-id keys.
- bd JMAP-zx3s.6 (main review): same uncertainty acknowledged in its calibration note — this finding pins the resolution.
title: on_success_update_email keys typed as Id but doc admits `#creationId` references — violates Id's RFC 8620 §1.2 alphabet contract
